الغَاذِيَةُ A certain vein; (K, TA;) so called because of its flowing with blood. (TA.) ―
-b2- And The part that is in a state of commotion, [or that pulses,] of the top of the head of a [young] child. as long as it continues soft; for when it becomes hard, and becomes bone, it is termed يَأْفُوخ: pl. الغَوَاذِى: mentioned by AZ: (TA:) also called الغَاذَّةُ. (IAar, K in art. غذ.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
